reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every type X equipped with a measurable space, every finite measure μ on X, and every measurable Markov kernel κ from X to X satisfying μ.bind κ = μ, there exists a continuous real-linear operator A : L²(X, μ; ℝ) → L²(X, μ; ℝ) with operator norm ‖A‖ ≤ 1 such that all the following hold simultaneously.
(1) For every function f : X → ℝ and every witness hf of MemLp f 2 μ (μ-almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L² norm), f is genuinely integrable with respect to κ(x, ·) for μ-almost every x; separately, the chosen representative of A(hf.toLp f) equals x ↦ ∫_X f(z) κ(x, dz) for μ-almost every x.
(2) For every u ∈ L²(X, μ; ℝ), if 0 ≤ u(x) for μ-almost every x, then 0 ≤ (A u)(x) for μ-almost every x, using the chosen representatives of these quotient classes.
(3) A sends the L² class of the constant-one function to itself: A[1] = [1].
(4) For every u ∈ L²(X, μ; ℝ), ∫_X (A u)(x) μ(dx) = ∫_X u(x) μ(dx).
(5) If κ is reversible with respect to μ, then A is self-adjoint: A* = A. Here reversibility means that, for every pair of measurable sets E and F in X, the nonnegative extended-real integral ∫⁻_{x ∈ E} κ(x, F) μ(dx) equals ∫⁻_{x ∈ F} κ(x, E) μ(dx).
The finite measure μ may have zero mass or any finite total mass; it need not be a probability measure. The Markov condition requires κ(x, ·) to be a probability measure for every x. Each almost-everywhere statement above is with respect to μ, with its displayed function parameters fixed; no common exceptional set for all functions is asserted. L² is the space of real square-integrable functions modulo μ-almost-everywhere equality. The integrals in (1) and (4) are real Bochner integrals with the totalized convention, and the genuine fiber integrability in (1) is a separate assertion.
objects: X is an arbitrary type with a measurable-space structure. μ is a finite measure on X. κ is a measurable kernel from X to X with every κ(x, ·) a probability measure; its invariance is μ.bind κ = μ. Lp ℝ 2 μ is the real Hilbert space of μ-square-integrable functions modulo μ-almost-everywhere equality. hf.toLp f denotes the class of a function with a MemLp witness. A is an existentially supplied continuous real-linear endomorphism of this Hilbert space; ‖A‖ is its operator norm. Coercions of Lp elements are chosen representatives. Lp.const 2 μ 1 is the constant-one class, and IsSelfAdjoint A says its Hilbert adjoint equals A.
domains: X has only the supplied measurable-space structure. μ ranges over measures on X of arbitrary finite nonnegative total mass, including zero. κ ranges over Markov kernels X → measures on X. Ordinary f ranges over all functions X → ℝ, subject to a supplied proof hf : MemLp f 2 μ; it need not be everywhere measurable. The positivity and integral-preservation variables range over all elements of Lp ℝ 2 μ. The fiber variable z and the integration/output variable x range over X. Reversibility quantifies over every pair of measurable subsets of X, using nonnegative extended-real kernel-mass integrals; A and the other integrals are real-valued/Hilbert-space objects.
quantifiers: The outer universal order is X, a measurable-space structure on X, μ, an IsFiniteMeasure μ instance, κ, an IsMarkovKernel κ instance, and an invariance proof hκ. Then one A is existentially quantified before all conclusion conjuncts. The representation conjunct is ∀ f : X → ℝ, ∀ hf : MemLp f 2 μ, ((∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Integrable f (κ x)) ∧ ((A (hf.toLp f) : X → ℝ) =ᵐ[μ] (fun x => ∫ z, f z ∂κ x))). The positivity conjunct is ∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 μ, ((∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 ≤ u x) → ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 ≤ A u x). Constant preservation is an equality without further quantification. Integral preservation is ∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 μ, equality of the two μ-integrals. Finally, κ.IsReversible μ → IsSelfAdjoint A is a conditional property of that same A.
assumptions: Only a measurable-space structure on X, finiteness of μ, the everywhere probability/Markov condition on κ, and κ-invariance of μ are unconditional hypotheses. There is no probability normalization of μ, nonzero-mass requirement, topological structure, countability condition, or pointwise measurability requirement on each represented ordinary f beyond MemLp. MemLp f 2 μ is local to the representation assertion for f. Nonnegativity μ-almost everywhere is the local premise of positivity for each Lp element. Reversibility is a further premise only for the self-adjointness conclusion: for all measurable E,F, ∫⁻_{x ∈ E} κ(x,F) μ(dx) = ∫⁻_{x ∈ F} κ(x,E) μ(dx).
conclusion: There exists a single continuous real-linear A on real L² with ‖A‖ ≤ 1, simultaneously satisfying: every MemLp function is integrable on μ-almost every kernel fiber and its class is mapped to the class represented μ-almost everywhere by its kernel integral; A preserves μ-almost-everywhere nonnegativity; A fixes the constant-one class; A preserves the μ-integral of every Lp element; and A is self-adjoint if κ is reversible. No uniqueness of A, converse to the reversible implication, or everywhere pointwise kernel representation is asserted.
scopes: All displayed almost-everywhere quantifiers use μ, never κ(x, ·). For fixed f and hf, the fiber-integrability assertion and the representative-equality assertion are separate μ-almost-everywhere assertions; their null sets may differ and may depend on those parameters. The statement supplies no one μ-conull set valid for every f. For each fixed u, both the positivity premise and conclusion have their own μ-almost-everywhere scope; the premise does not assert everywhere nonnegativity. Equality to the kernel-integral function is equality of representatives only μ-almost everywhere, whereas A[1] = [1] is equality in Lp. Integral preservation is an exact equality of real integrals for every u, not an almost-everywhere assertion. The reversible implication applies to the same A chosen before the conjunction and does not condition its existence or its other properties.
constant_dependencies: The Lp exponent 2, scalar field ℝ, norm bound 1, positivity threshold 0, and fixed function value 1 are fixed constants, not existential or data-dependent parameters. The contraction bound is exactly 1, independent of X, μ(X), and κ; no normalization factor involving μ(X) occurs. The witness A may depend on the fixed space, μ, κ, and supplied hypotheses, but is chosen uniformly before all functions and does not require reversibility. The constant-one class is available because μ is finite, including in the zero-measure case. Exceptional sets are not uniform across function parameters.
